articles.description:
Improvement
  
We've made some small but impactful changes to the Smily payment page. Enjoy an improved Meta title, a clearer display of discounts, better visibility of damage deposits, and a refined display of centimes. 
Check them out below:
The Meta title is now "Provide Payment Information" instead of "Smily"


Euro cents are now displayed in the same font as other digits


The damage deposit is no longer included in the balance amount due, but is displayed separately


Discounts are now displayed in negative, making it much clearer for guests when they're getting a great deal




Stay tuned for more improvements to the payment page, coming soon!
articles.title: Enhancements to the Smily Payment Page

articles.description:
New!
  
Discover how SmilyPay’s latest feature simplifies your financial reconciliation process!
We recently added a Finance section to Smily, to help you to track and reconcile your payouts from SmilyPay. 
Now, you can export the Completed Payouts Report from the Finance section as a CSV file. This new feature makes payment reconciliation quick and easy!
articles.title: New: export your SmilyPay payouts!

articles.author: Basile, Product Manager
articles.description:
New!
  
Are you looking to maximize your revenue and streamline your booking management? :) 
Smily is thrilled to announce the global release of our Non-Refundable Rate Synchronization feature with Booking.com now available directly from your Smily booking' app.
Why consider non-refundable rates?
Creating and managing non-refundable rates directly on Booking.com has always been a powerful strategy for securing guaranteed income. Now, with Smily's latest feature, you can set up these rates effortlessly, directly through the Smily interface, giving you more control and ease of setup.
Benefits of Non-Refundable Rates:
Secure more bookings: Attract guests who are sure about their travel plans by offering a percentage discount for non-refundable rates.
Reduce cancellations: Minimize the risk of last-minute cancellations, ensuring your earnings are protected.
Flexibility: Choose full or partial synchronization based on your needs, with the ability to manage multiple rates seamlessly.
How does it work?
Enable the Feature: 
Switch the non-refundable rates to "Yes" in your Smily settings under the Booking.com apps via the new "Non-Refundable option" in the Change Settings form of the property.


You can enable it by property or do a bulk edit from the button below > Apply for existing rentals.





Set Your Discount: Decide on the percentage discount for this rate, providing attractive pricing to your guests.


Synchronize and Go: Save your changes, and let Smily handle the synchronization with Booking.com using our new API integration.


Enable it today and start reaping the benefits!
Your Smily team
articles.title: Introducing non-refundable rate synchronization with Booking.com

articles.description:
Description: Potential for API credential disclosure over plaintext HTTP
What happened?
The Tailscale API is primarily accessible over TLS-encrypted HTTP at
api.tailscale.com. It also has a limited plaintext HTTP handler to serve HTTP
to HTTPS redirects.
Browsers that connect over plaintext HTTP do not send cookies marked as Secure
to prevent them from being disclosed to network intermediaries.
However, API clients that connect using plaintext HTTP and send requests
with authentication tokens in headers have no such protections to prevent
disclosure.
Before June 26, 2024, the Tailscale API did not reject credentialed plaintext
API requests and instead served them HTTP 302 redirects as it would to browsers.
Typical HTTP client libraries handle redirects transparently, and consequently, the user
would not necessarily know their credentials had been exposed.
Starting on June 26, 2024, the Tailscale API now returns errors for all plaintext
HTTP requests that include credentials. Additionally, the Tailscale API now
automatically revokes API keys that it observes sent over HTTP and notifies
Tailnet security owners of this action.
Who was affected?
Any Tailscale API client that connected over plaintext HTTP using credentials
before June 26, 2024.
What was the impact?
API clients that connected over plaintext HTTP before June 26, 2024 would have
exposed their credentials to network intermediaries, risking them to theft and
replay.
What do I need to do?
No action is needed at this time.
Credits
Thanks to Joachim Viide for reporting this issue.

Jul 11, 15:21 UTC
Resolved - On July 11, 2024, between 10:20 UTC and 14:00 UTC Copilot Chat was degraded and experienced intermittent timeouts. This only impacted requests routed to one of our service region providers. The error rate peaked at 10% for all requests and 9% of users. This was due to host upgrades in an upstream service provider. While this was a planned event, processes and tooling was not in place to anticipate and mitigate this downtime. 

We are working to improve our processes and tooling for future planned events and escalation paths with our upstream providers.

Resolved - On June 28th, 2024, at 16:06 UTC, a backend update by GitHub triggered a significant number of long-running Organization membership update jobs in our job processing system. articles.description:
Issue Summary:
On Thursday, July 11, 2024, from 12:10 PM PDT to 12:12 PM PDT, a number of users had trouble loading messages in Slack.

Our internal monitoring systems alerted us of the unexpected spike in error rates which prompted our incident response processes to begin. Through our investigation, we determined that a recent data migration caused an unexpected influx of client reloads, which temporarily overwhelmed the database responsible for servicing the affected API calls.

As a result, an automated safety measure temporarily paused traffic until the database returned to a healthy state. Once error rates returned to normal, users were no longer experiencing trouble.
articles.title: Incident: Intermittent performance issues using Slack

articles.description:
Issue summary:
From 7:13 PM PDT on July 2, 2024 to 2:38 PM PDT on July 3, 2024, some users experienced issues loading threads in Slack.

We traced the issue to one of our databases. Repeated API calls related to threads from one org caused the database responsible for storing that thread to become overwhelmed. This overload affected other users accessing the same database, causing congestion, which prevented them from using it effectively and created further unexpected timeouts.

As an immediate mitigation step, we halted all traffic from users using that API call in order to retrieve the thread from the database which allowed our systems to catch-up. Once traffic started flowing at a reasonable rate again, we reinstated the API call for all users and disallowed the thread that initially caused an issue. This resolved the issue for all impacted users.

We've now added additional code to the problematic thread to bypass this particular API so that any unwanted traffic congestion can be mediated.
articles.title: Incident: Issues loading threads

articles.description:
Issue Summary:
On June 24, 2024 from 11:25AM PDT to July 3, 2024 11:30AM PDT, users were unable to post in some channels due to an "Only some people can post" message on iOS as if the channel was made announcement-only. This initially was handled as a bug, however, the issue began to unexpectedly impact more users. Out of an abundance of caution, we promptly activated our incident response processes to expedite our investigation.

We determined this issue was presenting only temporarily for most users and was often resolved by switching channels, clearing app cache, or by force-closing the app and re-launching.

A fix was implemented in version 24.07.10 of the iOS app to restore channel posting functionality, resolving the issue for affected users. Updating the app is recommended in order to capture the fix.
articles.title: Incident: Issues sending messages to channels

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On July 2, 2024 from 5:09 PM PDT to 7:00 PM PDT, users may have experienced issues uploading files, sending messages with attached files, downloading files, and viewing files in conversations. 

A code change inadvertently introduced a logic error in our file handling processes. We reverted this code change, resolving the issue for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Issues with file uploads

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On July 1, 2024 from 12:23 PM PDT to around 5:20 PM PDT, some users experienced issued with loading threads, channels, direct messages, the Activity tab, and search results. Some users may have also experienced issues with sending messages. 

An error occurred during a routine database process. This error meant that a small subset of user requests were incorrectly routed to databases that did not exist. 

We made an immediate change to redirect user requests to cached data where possible to mitigate some of the errors. In parallel, we rebuilt the database mapping to correctly reroute the affected traffic. This resolved the issue for all users.
articles.title: Incident: Issues loading threads and activity feed

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On June 20, 2024 from 11:30 AM PDT to 11:50 AM PDT, some users were unable to load Slack and may have experienced a “We are unable to load your workspace” error message.

We made a backend update to one of our databases which unexpectedly caused that database to become overloaded, resulting in some users being unable to load Slack. We paused the update until error rates returned to normal, which resolved the issues for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Some users unable to connect to Slack

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On June 18, 2024 from 9:00 AM to 2:00 PM PDT, some users had trouble playing video clips on mobile.

Through investigation, we discovered a recent change to how recorded clips were stored when sent on desktop was causing compatibility issues when users attempted to play them on their mobile devices. Though, this change did not affect other file or media types.

We rolled out a fix which allowed these video files to save properly and play on mobile again.
articles.title: Incident: Video clips recorded on desktop fail to play on mobile

articles.description:
Issue summary:
From June 17, 2024, around 9:00 AM until 4:14 PM PDT, users experienced unexpected behaviors that prevented them from completing certain administrative actions, such as transferring workspace ownership, updating workspace retention settings, or reinstalling apps from the Slack App Directory.

We traced this back to an issue with our webpage UI code that prevented certain web elements from appearing or loading properly. These elements would prevent the action from completing. The problematic code was identified and we rolled out a fix to restore the full functionality of these pages.
articles.title: Incident: Some users may be unable to complete ownership transfers
